title: “All I Want” by Toad the Wet Sprocket
text: "All I Want" is a song by American alternative rock band Toad the Wet Sprocket, released by Columbia Records in 1992 as the second single from their third album, Fear. "All I Want" reached number 15 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and number 10 on the US Cash Box Top 100.

title: “When a Man Loves a Woman” by Michael Bolton
text: "When a Man Loves a Woman" is a song written by Calvin Lewis and Andrew Wright and first recorded by the American singer Percy Sledge in 1966 at Norala Sound Studio in Sheffield, Alabama. It made number one on both the US Billboard Hot 100 and Cash Box Top 100, as well as on the Billboard R&B singles chart.

title: “I Can't Dance” by Genesis
text: "I Can't Dance" is the fourth track from English rock band Genesis' 14th studio album, We Can't Dance. It was released in December 1991 by Virgin Records as the second single from the record.

title: “Hazard” by Richard Marx
text: "Hazard" is a song written, produced, and performed by American singer-songwriter Richard Marx. The song is about a woman named Mary who mysteriously disappears and a social pariah who is accused of orchestrating Mary's disappearance, despite claiming to be innocent.

title: “Mysterious Ways” by U2
text: "Mysterious Ways" is a song by Irish rock band U2. It is the eighth track from their seventh album, Achtung Baby, and was released as the album's second single on 2 December 1991 by Island Records, two weeks after the album.

title: “Too Funky” by George Michael
text: "Too Funky" is a song written and performed by English singer and songwriter George Michael and released by Columbia Records in the United States and Epic Records elsewhere in 1992. The song was Michael's final single for his recording contract with Sony Music before he started legal action to extricate himself from it.

title: “How Do You Talk to an Angel” by The Heights
text: "How Do You Talk to an Angel" is a song written by Steve Tyrell, Barry Coffing, and Stephanie Tyrell. It was the theme for the American TV series The Heights.

title: “One” by U2
text: "One" is a song by Irish rock band U2. It is the third track from their seventh album, Achtung Baby, and it was released as the record's third single on 24 February 1992.

title: “Keep on Walkin'” by CeCe Peniston
text: "Keep On Walkin'" is a song by American musician CeCe Peniston, recorded for her debut album, Finally, on A&M Records. Written by Steve Hurley, Marc Williams and Kym Sims, it was released in May 1992 as the singer's third single from the album and was her third number one on the US Billboard Hot Dance Music/Club Play chart.

title: “Hold on My Heart” by Genesis
text: "Hold on My Heart" is a song by English rock band Genesis from their 14th studio album, We Can't Dance. The ballad was released as the album's third single on 6 April 1992 by Virgin Records.

title: “The Way I Feel About You” by Karyn White
text: "The Way I Feel About You" is a song by American R&B singer-songwriter Karyn White. It was released on November 7, 1991, by Warner and Flyte Tyme, from her second album, Ritual of Love.

title: “Warm It Up” by Kris Kross
text: "Warm It Up" is a song by American hip-hop duo Kris Kross, released in June 1992 by Ruffhouse and Columbia Records as the second single from their debut album, Totally Krossed Out. Written and produced by Jermaine Dupri, the song was released as the follow-up to the duo's multi-platinum chart topping hit, "Jump" on June 4.

title: “In the Closet” by Michael Jackson
text: "In the Closet" is a song by the American singer Michael Jackson, released on April 13, 1992, by Epic Records, as the third single from his eighth album, Dangerous. It was written and produced by Jackson and Teddy Riley.

title: “Friday I'm in Love” by The Cure
text: "Friday I'm in Love" is a song by British rock band the Cure. Released in May 1992 by Fiction Records as the second single from their ninth studio album, Wish, the song became a worldwide hit, reaching number six in the UK and number 18 in the United States, where it also topped the Billboard Modern Rock Tracks chart.

title: “Everything About You” by Ugly Kid Joe
text: "Everything About You" is a song by American heavy metal band Ugly Kid Joe, originally from their 1991 EP, As Ugly as They Wanna Be. The pop-metal song gained popularity after being featured in the 1992 hit film Wayne's World and was later included on the band's full-length debut album, America's Least Wanted, which was also released in 1992.

title: “Rhythm Is a Dancer” by Snap!
text: "Rhythm Is a Dancer" is a song by German Eurodance group Snap!, released in March 1992 by Arista and Logic Records as the second single from their second studio album, The Madman's Return. It features vocals by American singer Thea Austin.

title: “Missing You Now” by Michael Bolton
text: "Missing You Now" is a song by American singer-songwriter Michael Bolton. It was released in December 1991 by Columbia Records as the fourth single from his seventh album, Time, Love & Tenderness, and features saxophone player Kenny G. The track was co-produced by Walter Afanasieff, who co-wrote the song with Bolton and Diane Warren.

title: “Back to the Hotel” by N2Deep
text: "Back to the Hotel" is a song by American hip hop duo N2Deep. It is the lead single from their debut studio album of the same name and their most successful song, peaking at number 14 on the Billboard Hot 100.

title: “Everything Changes” by Kathy Troccoli

title: In Dubăsari, Moldova, escalating tensions turn into open hostilities and the beginning of the Transnistria War.
text: Dubăsari or Dubossary (Russian: Дубоссары; Ukrainian: Дубоcсари; Yiddish: דובאסאר) is a city in Transnistria, with a population of 23,650. Claimed by both the Republic of Moldova and the unrecognized Pridnestrovian Moldavian Republic, the city is under the latter's administration, and functions as the seat of the Dubăsari District.

title: The Supreme Court of Algeria bans the Islamic Salvation Front, which is poised to win control of the Parliament of Algeria in runoff elections.
text: The Parliament of Algeria is the legislative assembly of Algeria.

title: Mauritius becomes a republic while remaining a member of the Commonwealth of Nations.
text: A republic, based on the Latin phrase res publica, is a state in which political power rests with the public (people), typically through their representatives—in contrast to an absolute monarchy or a direct democracy. Although a republic is most often a single sovereign state, subnational state entities that have governments that are republican in nature may be referred to as republics.

title: The 6.7 .mw-parser-output .tooltip-dotted{border-bottom:1px dotted;cursor:help}Mw Erzincan earthquake affects eastern Turkey with a maximum Mercalli intensity of VIII (Severe), killing 498–652 and injuring around 2,000.
text: The Modified Mercalli intensity scale measures the effects of an earthquake at a given location. This is in contrast with the seismic magnitude usually reported for an earthquake.

title: White South Africans vote in favour of political reforms which will end the apartheid regime and create a power-sharing multi-racial government.
text: White South Africans are South Africans of European descent. In linguistic, cultural, and historical terms, they are generally divided into the Afrikaans-speaking descendants of the Dutch East India Company's original colonists, known as Afrikaners, and the Anglophone descendants of predominantly British colonists of South Africa.

title: In French regional elections, the conservative Rally for the Republic and the centre-right Union for French Democracy win in a landslide, capturing 20 of 22 metropolitan regional presidencies.
text: Regional elections were held in France on 22 March 1992. At stake were the presidencies of each of France's 26 régions, which, although lacking legislative autonomy, manage sizeable budgets.

title: STS-45: Space Shuttle Atlantis takes off from Cape Canaveral carrying instruments designed to study global warming.
text: STS-45 was a 1992 NASA Space Shuttle mission using the Space Shuttle Atlantis. Its almost nine-day scientific mission was with a non-deployable payload of instruments.

title: The Treaty on Open Skies is signed in Helsinki, Finland, to establish a program of unarmed surveillance flights over the 34 member states. It went into effect on January 1, 2002.
text: The Treaty on Open Skies establishes a program of unarmed aerial surveillance flights over the entire territory of its participants. The treaty is designed to enhance mutual understanding and confidence by giving all participants, regardless of size, a direct role in gathering information about military forces and activities of concern to them.

title: The Shot (Duke–Kentucky): In what Sports Illustrated deemed the greatest college basketball game of all time, Christian Laettner sinks an overtime buzzer-beater to advance Duke to their fifth straight Final Four.
text: The 1992 NCAA tournament was highlighted by a game between #1 seed Duke and #2 seed Kentucky in the East Region final to determine a spot in the Final Four. With 2.1 seconds remaining in overtime, defending national champion Duke trailed 103–102.

title: The Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act of Singapore comes into force.
text: The Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act 1990 is a Singapore statute which, according to its long title, provides for the maintenance of religious harmony, for the establishment of a Presidential Council for Religious Harmony ("PCRH"), and for matters connected therewith. title: The Assembly of Bosnia and Herzegovina (without the presence of Serb political delegates) proclaims independence from the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
text: Serbs, are a South Slavic ethnic group and nation who share a common Serbian ancestry, culture, history, and language. They live primarily in their nation-state of Serbia, and in neighboring Bosnia and Herzegovina, Montenegro, Croatia, and Kosovo, with smaller communities in North Macedonia, Romania, and Hungary, while also constituting a significant diaspora with communities across Europe, the Americas, and Oceania.
